items.title: Section: Five Ways Beings Act Mad Without Being Mad

items.zh: 復次，經言：汝等長夜增羯吒斯，恒受血滴。何等名為羯吒斯耶？所謂貪愛。貪愛之言，與羯吒斯名差別也。此言顯示攝受集諦。恒受血滴，攝受苦諦。復次，婆羅門喻經中，世尊依死雜染說如是言：有五非狂，如狂所作。何等為五？一、解支節者。謂更有餘活命方便，而樂分析所有支節以自活命。是名第一非狂如狂所作。二、慳貪者。謂慳貪所蔽，慳貪因緣所獲財寶，不食不施，唯除命終，欻然虛棄大寶庫藏。是名第二非狂如狂所作。三、樂生天者。謂更有餘身語意攝種種妙行生天方便，而樂妄執投火、溺水、顛墜高崖自害身命作生天因。是名第三非狂如狂所作。四、樂解脫者。謂更有餘八支聖道解脫方便，而樂妄執自逼自惱種種苦行作解脫因。是名第四非狂如狂所作。五、傷悼死者。謂依傷悼亡者因緣，種種哀歎剺攫其身，坌灰拔髮，斷食自毀，欲令亡者還復如故。是名第五非狂如狂所作。
items.en: Moreover, in the Brāhmaṇa Simile Sutra, the Blessed One, speaking of rebirth defilement, said this: there are five things not madness, yet carried out as madness would carry them out. What are the five? First, dismembering the limbs — though other means of livelihood remain, delighting in dismembering the limbs of bodies to sustain one's own life. This is the first thing not mad, yet carried out as madness. Second, miserliness — covered by miserliness, neither eating nor giving away wealth gained through it, only at death suddenly abandoning great treasuries. This is the second. Third, delighting in heavenly rebirth — though other wholesome means of body, speech, and mind remain, delighting in the false conviction that throwing oneself into fire, drowning, or falling from a cliff is the cause of heavenly rebirth. This is the third. Fourth, delighting in liberation — though the noble eightfold path remains as the means, delighting in the false conviction that self-inflicted austerity is the cause of liberation. This is the fourth. Fifth, mourning the dead — cutting the flesh, covering oneself in ashes, pulling out hair, fasting and self-harm, hoping to restore the departed to life. This is the fifth.

items.title: Section: A Mother Becomes a Wife — The Verse on Saṃsāra's Endless Shuffle

items.zh: 世間無決定，顛倒謂為我父母及妻孥、兄弟、親友等。曾母轉為妻，妻復為兒婦，兒婦轉為婢，或作怨家妻。曾父轉為子，子復為怨敵，怨敵復為奴，或為僕隸等。曾王轉為臣，臣復為貧匱，或閭邑下賤，為世所輕鄙。曾作婆羅門，展轉為三姓，或復旃荼羅，及補羯娑等。於無量百千那庾多往返，為父復為子，及怨家等身。如幻士眾中，示種種形類，異生處流轉，現多身亦爾。煩惱業緣因，令種種諸行，數數而積集，如幻化所起。雖遭是眾幻，然無智所覆，常於諸行中，樂著曾無厭。既自幻惑已，坌灰泣傷歎；於不應憂悲，橫生諸悲惱。離假名親屬，種種自憂悲；棄捐正法行，舉手而號泣。癡憍慢所亂，數行諸放逸。如是等種類，廣說遍應知。
items.en: The world has nothing fixed; deluded, beings grasp a self, calling others father, mother, spouse, child, sibling, and friend. A former mother becomes a wife; that wife becomes a daughter-in-law; that daughter-in-law becomes a servant, or an enemy's own wife. A former father becomes a son; that son becomes an enemy; that enemy becomes a servant or slave. A former king becomes a minister; that minister becomes destitute; or is born into a low, despised quarter, scorned by the world. Affliction and karma, as cause and condition, give rise to formations of every kind, accumulated again and again, arising just as illusions do. Though meeting this vast illusion, covered by a lack of wisdom, beings constantly delight in these very formations, never once growing weary. Already deluded by their own illusion, they cover themselves in ash and weep in sorrow, generating needless grief where none was ever truly called for. Parting from merely nominal kin, generating all manner of private sorrow, they abandon the practice of the true Dharma, raising their hands and wailing. Disturbed by delusion and pride, indulging again and again in heedlessness — such kinds as these should be broadly understood in full.

items.title: Section: Twelve Links, Five Aspects — Ignorance's Own Portrait Begins

items.zh: 復次，鬪諍劫中有四過失。謂壽量衰退、安樂衰退、功德衰退、一切世間盛事衰退。復次，鬪諍劫中諸有情類，略於八處互不相數。一、不數正法，二、不數名聞，三、不數宗族，四、不數可愍，五、不數善友，六、不數有德，七、不數有恩，八、不數親友。問：先說生雜染中，無明緣行乃至生緣老死，此無明等十二支差別義，云何應知？答：略由五相。一、由相故；二、由自性故；三、由業故；四、由法故；五、由因果故。問：何等為無明相？答：貪、瞋、慢相是無明相，計我我所相、無慚無愧相、多放逸相、性羸鈍相、饒睡眠相、心愁慼相、種種惡業現行等相，是無明相。
items.en: Moreover, in the kalpa of strife, there are four faults: decline of lifespan, decline of happiness, decline of merit, and decline of every flourishing worldly circumstance. Moreover, in the kalpa of strife, beings, in brief, disregard one another across eight areas: not valuing the correct Dharma, not valuing reputation, not valuing kinship, not valuing compassion, not valuing good friends, not valuing virtue, not valuing kindness received, and not valuing friendship. Question: as already explained regarding rebirth defilement, ignorance conditioning formations down through birth conditioning old age and death, how should the differences among these twelve links of ignorance and the rest be understood? Answer: in brief, through five aspects. First, through characteristic marks. Second, through intrinsic nature. Third, through function. Fourth, through classification into dharmas. Fifth, through cause and effect. What are the marks of ignorance? Answer: the marks of greed, hatred, and conceit are marks of ignorance; the mark of computing self and what belongs to self, the mark of shamelessness and lack of conscience, the mark of pervasive heedlessness, the mark of weak and dull nature, the mark of excessive sleep, the mark of sorrowful distress, and the mark of manifesting every kind of unwholesome deed, are all marks of ignorance.

items.zh: 問：何等是無明自性？答：自性總相，如前已說。自性差別，今當顯示。謂或有隨眠無明，或有覺悟無明，或有煩惱共行無明，或有不共獨行無明，或有蔽伏心性無明，或有發業無明，或有不染污無明，或有離羞恥無明，或有堅固無明。謂無般涅槃法者所有無明。問：何等為無明業？答：

blocks.text: Five kinds of behaviour that look sane but are a kind of madness, a verse on the endless shuffling of family ties, and the start of a fresh account of the twelve links.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a miser neither enjoys wealth nor gives it, living like a pauper. Some do good deeds hoping for heaven out of deluded wrong view. Not knowing the eightfold path, some torment themselves hoping to bring back the dead.

Master Cháng Bǎi: nothing in the world is fixed; parents, spouse, and children are temporary conditions of this life. With birth there is death, yet beings grieve where grief cannot help, and for merely nominal kin abandon the practice of the Dharma.

Five aspects frame the rest of the fascicle. Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging to the aggregates as self comes from not penetrating no-self; weak faculties make practice hard. (Untranslated, 0637a16: ignorance is of many kinds: latent or awake, with afflictions or alone, obscuring the mind, generating karma, undefiled, shameless, firm.)
The verse on kin shifting across lives is meant to loosen grief, not love. Care for family is right; grief that abandons the path is the madness.

quiz.q: What are the five things not mad yet done as if mad?
options: dismembering, miserliness, delight in heaven, delight in liberation, and mourning the dead
greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, and views, afflictions making beings seem mad, unrelated to austerity or mourning
deficiency, madness, distraction, nature, clinging
desire, ill will, harm, family, homeland
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: these five are not madness yet act like it; a miser neither enjoys wealth nor gives it, living like a pauper; dismembering bodies for a living is what fools pursue and the wise leave. The English is accurate.

quiz.q: What is wrong with those delighting in heavenly rebirth?
options: wishing heaven is itself wrong, even by good deeds, only liberation being right
wholesome deeds exist as means, yet they hold fire, drowning, and falling to be the cause
they lack wealth
they pray to the wrong god
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though there are good deeds of body, speech, and mind leading to heaven, such acts come from deluded wrong view, unmad yet like madness. The fault is in the means, not in the aim. The English keeps this.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe those delighting in liberation and those mourning?
options: exemplary austerity and filial piety, the passage in fact praising them
not knowing the eightfold path, tormenting themselves; hoping to revive the dead
both want heaven
both want wealth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: not knowing the eightfold path as the way to liberation, one falsely clings to self-torment; hoping thereby to bring the dead back, one acts as if mad. The English drops 種種哀歎 from the fifth, so the idea of lament is lost.

quiz.q: What is the theme of the verse "the world has nothing fixed"?
options: gods decide all, kinship is fixed and to be cherished
one should seek wealth
kin and rank change endlessly, illusory, and needless grief should not arise
one should leave kin
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: nothing in the world is fixed; parents, spouse, and children are temporary conditions of this life; with birth there is death, yet beings grieve where grief does not belong. The source has three further stanzas the English lacks.

quiz.q: The English has "they abandon the practice of the true path." What is the problem?
options: no problem: 正法 is the eightfold path, chosen for sound, the lecture agreeing
it should be "true king"
正法 should be "true Dharma"; "path" blurs it with 道
it should be "true law court"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: for merely nominal kin one uselessly abandons the practice of the true Dharma, only raising one's hands and wailing. Elsewhere the English consistently uses Dharma for 法, so "true path" stands out. "Merely nominal kin" is a fine rendering of 假名親屬.

quiz.q: Is §27 ("he came without regret...") treatise text, and how does this bank treat it?
options: yes: it is the prose after the verse, the Buddha's own words
no: the whole section is the lecturer's aside and a Śakra story, not cited as treatise
it is from the Consciousness-Only treatise
it is the Sub-commentary
quiz.why: The passage does not appear among the treatise lines in the lecture. Master Cháng Bǎi introduces it as further examples of the unmad acting mad, and then tells a story. The treatise goes straight on to the kalpa of strife. So it is an insertion in both Chinese and English.

quiz.q: What are the four faults of the kalpa of strife?
options: decline of lifespan, happiness, merit, and worldly flourishing
growth of greed, hatred, delusion, and conceit, lifespan and happiness declining only in the next kalpa
imbalance of the elements
four kinds of clinging
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: at this time the ten evils flourish, people steal from each other, and there is no harmony, and so happiness declines; to be free of evil and affliction is 功, and many complete good deeds 德. The English "merit" for 功德 is fine.

quiz.q: The English renders 不數 as "not valuing" throughout. How does this compare with the lecture?
options: the same: the lecture says 不數 means not valuing reputation or kindness received
the English lists only seven
the English lists nine
the lecture reads no mutual exchange, as not praising or helping; "kindness received" reverses direction
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi calls these eight tendencies 互不相數, and for reputation says people will not praise each other's real virtues. So the term is mutual and active. "Not valuing reputation" makes it a personal attitude. This follows the lecture only; other readings of 數 may exist.

quiz.q: Through which five aspects are the twelve links distinguished?
options: the four truths and their total mark, marks and nature being Yogācāra additions
marks, nature, function, classification, and cause and effect
three times, cause, result
affliction, karma, suffering, birth, death
quiz.why: The five are the frame for the rest of this fascicle. The whole passage on intrinsic nature is missing from both Chinese and English, so §29 jumps to function. Master Cháng Bǎi on marks: these afflictions arise from failing to penetrate things, blind to reality.

quiz.q: Why are greed, hatred, conceit, and computing self marks of ignorance?
options: one factor with several names, dullness and sleep being health matters
all belong to the higher realms
all are wholesome
all arise from not penetrating, not seeing no-self; dull faculties block the path
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: clinging to the aggregates as self comes from not penetrating no-self; weak and dull faculties of faith and the rest make practice hard, obstructing the path. Marks are how ignorance shows itself in behaviour. The English follows.
